<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/seed.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/seed.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via SeedSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/seed.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/seed.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `34bed4eb30e483339580a7c619c9066e915f1b99` — the merge of head `cc0a04bff73226fd76034146fa72cf4f781d0e8d` into base `958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 34bed4eb30e483339580a7c619c9066e915f1b99 && git checkout 34bed4eb30e483339580a7c619c9066e915f1b99
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d cc0a04bff73226fd76034146fa72cf4f781d0e8d && git checkout -B drift-repro 958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d && git merge --no-ff cc0a04bff73226fd76034146fa72cf4f781d0e8d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 958ee03594968c651db1bc40ecb05bfe72f94b2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 review · REWORK (PR body only; the code is accepted)** · Head-sha: `e020dc236a1382a92d367873881066f16f01a396` · card #34940 · read 2026-11-18T02:05Z

This is a full review: there is no earlier L1 record. I read the whole diff from merge-base `743308b9` (14 files, +689 / -27; 11 commits, one of them a main merge), the claim 6963214228 and dev reports 6966124515 and 6966753013. Seat rulings: route A, Q1 = B, Q2.

**Schema** (`seed.zod.ts`).
- `fallback: z.literal(true).optional()` is added, and so is `.refine(dependentRequired({ fallback: ['locale'] }), { path: ['fallback'] })`.
- Through the closed projection list, the published JSON Schema says `dependentRequired` instead of accepting what the parse refuses.
- The refine keeps the object's `.shape`, and the existing readers (`SeedSchema.shape.mode`/`externalId` in metadata-core, cloud-connection and seed-loader.zod) still typecheck at this head.
- `locale`'s describe gains the "unless one is marked `fallback: true`" clause.
- The spec pins cover: kept, absent means no key, refused without `locale` at the key with the fix, only `true`, and `defineSeed` carrying it.

**Loader** (`seed-loader.ts`).
- `load()` now runs `filterByEnv`, then `findDuplicateFallbackSets` on the env-kept datasets, then `filterByLocale`.
- A duplicate is refused through `buildResult` with one `field: 'fallback'` error per object. That happens before the landed-key record opens or any row is written, the same way the `dependsOn` refusal is returned.
- `filterByLocale` keeps a marked dataset that the locale would drop only when `objectsWithLocaleMatch` finds no locale-scoped dataset of its object listing the locale. Unscoped datasets neither match nor block.
- A load with no locale returns every dataset on its first line, as before.
- The info line names each fallback that loaded.
- The 15 loader pins cover selection, the unmarked control, the case-insensitive match, its own locales, the neutral set, per-object judging, the log, no locale, env both ways, the duplicate refusal at any locale, one per object, and split envs. The 11 runtime pins hit every locale producer (boot, hot reload, replay through setting and founder, install, reseed, heal) on the rows that reach the engine, each with an unmarked control.
- The body reports that ablating the fallback branch turns 7 loader and 7 runtime tests red. I did not re-run it.

**Ledgers and docs.**
- The `seed.fallback` row is `live`, with the consumer named by function and the producers shared with `locale`. The counts move from 19 to 20, and the authorable-surface row is added.
- The generated references are regenerated, and `seed-data.mdx` gains its section.
- The skills hunk is gone after Q1 = B: `seeds.md` matches main at this head, and no `skills/**` path is in the diff.

**Paper.**
- Clause-② yes (widening) and `Metadata-protocol: added`, with spec and metadata-protocol both `minor`. That is what an authorable-surface row requires.
- `runtime` changes in tests only.
- `check-governed-merges` says not governed.
- It is a widening, so no dogfood battery is owed.
- **Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** 0 failed, 58 success, 12 skipped, nothing running.

### Should-fix (blocks; paper only)

- **S1: `Skills-docs:` names no card.** The body reads "Skills-docs: follow-up owed (domain:skills child card, filed by triage)". That card now exists: #35070 ("skills objectstack-data seeds.md: name Seed.locale and Seed.fallback in the field table…"). The L1 checklist wants `Skills-docs: follow-up #N`, so that the debt Q1 = B moved out has a number on the record. Change the line to `Skills-docs: follow-up #35070`. This is a body edit only. Once it is done I will turn this into a same-head ACCEPT.

### For the seat's contract review (not a finding)

- **How far the duplicate refusal reaches.** `findDuplicateFallbackSets` judges the request's whole env-kept dataset list. The marketplace plugin's own per-organization replayer (`buildSeedReplayer`) builds that list from every installed package's datasets. So two packages that each mark a fallback set of the same object, or one package carrying a duplicate, would refuse that organization's seed for every package, unrelated objects included. Q2 ruled a load-time refusal enough. Whether that holds for a multi-package list, or should be scoped per package, belongs to the contract face. Stack-level detection with `os validate` is already named as a possible follow-up in the body.

**Owed, for the seat:** the contract review (Clause-② yes, `added`). Its face is `SeedSchema.fallback` and its `dependentRequired` projection, and the loader's selection and refusal contract. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e020dc236a1382a92d367873881066f16f01a396`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/spec/liveness/seed.json

Read: card #34940 (body, comments 6956175603, 6963214228, 6966124515, 6966753013), PR #35065 (body, file list, comments 6966126603, 6966814360, 6966829726), the net diff from merge-base `743308b9` (14 files, +689 / -27), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/seed-datasets.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/seed-locale.ts`, `packages/plugins/organizations/src/organizations-plugin.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts`.

Security-touching: no

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, schema: widened by one optional key. Right.** `SeedSchema` is a `strictObject`, so before this head `fallback` was an unknown key and refused. Every value accepted before is accepted now. The new refine (`dependentRequired({ fallback: ['locale'] })`) can only fire on a value carrying `fallback`, which no previously valid seed carries.
- **Accept-set, loader: no previously loading request is refused. Right.** `findDuplicateFallbackSets` fires only on two datasets with `fallback === true`; a request without the key takes the same `filterByEnv` then `filterByLocale` path as `filterDatasets` did, and `filterByLocale` returns the same kept set when no dataset is marked.
- **Published JSON Schema: carries the rule. Right.** `dependentRequired` is on the closed projection list (`refinement-projection.ts`, the `dependent-required` arm), so the parse and the published schema name the same dependency and the dropped-refinements baseline does not grow.
- **Authorable-surface baseline: one row added, `data/Seed:fallback`. Right.**
- **Liveness ledger: `seed.fallback` recorded `live`, counts 19 to 20. Right** under ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove: the key has one read (`isFallbackDataset`), a consumer that changes which rows reach the engine (`filterByLocale`), and the producers are the `locale` row's own. The row's stated bound ("live exactly where `locale` is") is accurate.
- **Generated references: match the schema.** `seed.mdx`, `seed-loader.mdx`, `package-api.mdx` and `manifest.mdx` each gain the `fallback` row with the schema's describe text verbatim, type `true`, optional, and the amended `locale` sentence.
- **Public TypeScript surface: `SeedSchema` is now a refined object.** `.shape` is kept and the four in-repo `.shape` readers typecheck on this head (check-runs green). No in-repo caller uses `.pick`, `.omit` or `.extend` on it. Named, not graded: an out-of-repo caller that does would be affected, as with every other schema already on the projection list.
- **Behaviour on the shared per-organization replay list: wrong.** See M1.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). Holds: one new optional authorable key, nothing previously accepted refused.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is the right kind (a new key an author can write), and the kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves. The changeset carries `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, both declaration lines, and matches the PR body. `@objectstack/runtime` changes in a test file only and is correctly absent. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev Q1 (keep or split the skills hunk): answered B and applied.** No `skills/**` path is in the diff at this head; the body reads `Skills-docs: follow-up #35070`, which also closes L1-e's paper finding on 6966814360 as far as the body goes.
- **Dev Q2 and L1-e's question (how far the duplicate refusal reaches): the load-time refusal is not enough on a multi-package list.** Graded below as M1 and S1. A cross-package collision is reachable, and so is a same-package one that needs no authoring mistake at all.
- **Deviation, `Metadata-protocol:` prose on the claim:** the PR body and changeset carry the closed kind. Accepted.
- **Deviation, generated files outside the literal surface:** they are what the generators emit for a new key and their gates are green. Accepted.
- **Deviation, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally:** the head's check-runs answer it. 64 success, 14 skipped, 0 failed, nothing running, at read time.
- **Out-of-scope note, stack-level authoring detection:** not owed by this PR; see S1 for why it would not replace a scoped loader check.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no join; the selection runs over the in-memory dataset list of the request.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts`** against the route A ruling and its first consumer.

The key, its literal-`true` value, the `dependentRequired` refusal at the `fallback` path and the describe text agree with the ruling (explicit per-set marker, additive, opt-in) and with what `filterByLocale` does. The jsdoc sentences on matching, `env` ordering, own-locale loading and the no-locale load each hold in the loader. The sentence "At most one per object in a load ... the load is refused" is implemented as written, and that sentence is where the design breaks at its first multi-package consumer.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`** against the contract.

Selection is correct sentence by sentence: `objectsWithLocaleMatch` counts only locale-scoped datasets among the env-kept ones, an unscoped set neither matches nor blocks, a marked set loads for its own locales through the first branch, and a load with no locale returns its input on the first line. The refusal returns through `buildResult` before the landed-key record opens.

M1 (must-fix) — a correctly authored fallback set refuses every later organization's seed after an ordinary reseed or upgrade.

- `findDuplicateFallbackSets` counts marked datasets per object across the whole request, with no notion of which package or which declaration a dataset came from.
- Both per-organization replayers hand the loader the shared `seed-datasets` list: `buildSeedReplayer` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:2360`) and the AppPlugin replayer (`app-plugin.ts`, `readSeedDatasets(ctx)`).
- That list is append-only. `mergeSeedDatasets` (`runtime/src/seed-datasets.ts:72`) is a plain `push` with no de-duplication, and nothing removes a package's datasets.
- `applySideEffects` merges a package's datasets on every call (`:7487`), and it is called by the boot rehydrate (`:1986`), the install and upgrade route (`:3586`) and the sample-data reseed (`:6290`).
- So in any running process, one reseed of an installed package (the rehydrate merged it once at boot, the reseed merges it again), or an install followed by a reseed or an upgrade, leaves two copies of that package's datasets in the list. If the package marks one set `fallback: true`, the list now holds two marked sets of that object.
- The reseed's own inline seed is unaffected, because it loads only that package's datasets, so the operator sees a successful reseed.
- Every organization founded afterwards, until the process restarts, gets no seed row from any package: the replay returns `success: false` with one `field: 'fallback'` error. The consumer (`organizations-plugin.ts`, `replayOrganizationSeed`) reports it as an info line, `per-org seed replay for ORG: +0 inserted, 0 updated, 1 error(s)`, and no fallback path follows.
- Before this head a doubled list was benign for `ignore` and `upsert` datasets (the second copy skips). The package the card is written for (a marketplace package with a locale-split price book) is exactly the one that will mark a fallback set, and it turns "ja-JP gets no price book" into "no organization gets any sample data".
- The ruling's condition (2) asks for the key to be enforced end to end at install, reseed, heal and replay. The replay leg does not hold once the list has been merged twice. No pin covers a replay after a second merge.
- The fix is the seat's to route. Options seen while reading: judge duplicates among distinct declarations rather than raw list entries; scope the refusal to the object instead of the load; or de-duplicate the shared list where it is merged, which is outside this claim's file surface.

S1 (should-fix) — the refusal's reach is the whole load, across packages, and it is quiet at the replay.

- This is L1-e's question as asked. Seed object names are used as-is with no package qualification (`app-plugin.ts`, "no FQN expansion"), so two installed packages can each seed the same object, and if each marks a fallback set the union is refused. Reachable; it needs two authors to mark the same object, so rarer than M1.
- What the user sees is the same as M1: the new organization is created with no seed rows of any package, unrelated objects included, and the only trace is the info line above. Neither package's own install or `os validate` would show it, because each package is valid alone; a stack-level authoring check would not catch it either.
- The Q2 ruling ("the load-time refusal is enough") reads as made for one package's datasets. For the shared list the refusal should be scoped (per object at least, so unrelated datasets still load) and the replay consumer should not report a refused seed at info. Whether scoping per package is wanted is a seat ruling.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the Q1 = B and Q2 ruling of 2026-11-18T01:25Z is quoted in the PR body and in the dev's delta report, but no comment on the card or the PR carries the ruling itself. It was judged here from those quotations.
- N2 (nit) — `refuseDuplicateFallbackSets` fills `recordIndex: 0` and `targetField: '(dataset)'` in a `ReferenceResolutionError`, a shape made for row-level errors; a consumer that renders `recordIndex` will point at a row that was never attempted. The `dependsOn` refusal already does the same.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34940-seed-locale-fallback`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

**L1 delta review · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `09232b7d0c3a274d493741b066110e652b20a083` · card #34940 · read 2026-11-18T03:24Z

This reviews the delta from L1 6966854128 (ACCEPT at `e020dc23`). The delta is fix round 2, `f64d23ed` (11 files, +182 / -65), done to the seat's ruling on the contract review of `e020dc23`, plus `09232b7d`, a main merge. Dev report 6968061404.

- **The merge is pure.** `git merge-tree --write-tree f64d23ed dcbb3633` equals `09232b7d`'s tree (`0b1b8349`).
- **Identical copies count once.** `findDuplicateFallbackSets` now groups the marked datasets of each object by `seedDeclarationFingerprint`: every key except the `_`-prefixed runtime envelope, serialised with sorted keys at every depth. Only two or more *distinct* declarations refuse. A package's list merged twice into the shared replay list no longer refuses every new organization's seed. Two packages that mark different sets of one object are still two declarations, which is right because object names are global.
- **The refusal is scoped to the object.** The refused object's marked datasets are filtered out before `filterByLocale`. Its unmarked datasets and every other object still seed.
  - The errors (`field: 'fallback'`, one per object) join `allErrors` (declared at 1288), so the result reads `success: false`.
  - Each refusal is logged once at `warn`, because an object's rows go visibly missing and a replay's consumer may report errors at `info` only.
  - An all-filtered load still returns the errors and not an empty success.
  - A load later refused for `dependsOn` keeps them, via `unshift`.
- **Pins.** The two refusal cases are re-stated to the new answer (only that object's marked sets go, and the rest seeds), with no silent deletion. Four new cases (two loader, two runtime) cover a list merged twice, which seeds normally, and two packages with different sets, which refuse only that object. The schema describe, the jsdoc, `seed-data.mdx`, the generated references, the liveness note and the changeset all follow the new rule.
- **Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** 0 failed, 55 success, 12 skipped, 2 still running. The local `dispatch-gates` run was stopped at the wind-down with 20 families unrun, so CI is the reading of record. No battery is owed for a widening.

No findings.

**Note for the seat's contract-review delta (not a finding):** a refused object loses *all* its marked sets, including for the locales those sets list themselves. An `en` organization gets neither `en` set when two packages both mark their `en` set as the fallback. That is what the describe now states ("none of that object's marked datasets loads"). It is the stricter reading of "no single choice", and it is the seat's to keep.

**Owed, for the seat:** the contract-review delta for `e020dc23..09232b7d`. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.
